docs.title: go-encryptions
docs.text:
Pure-Go encryption primitives, with no cgo.

The org fills gaps that the Go standard library and golang.org/x/crypto leave open, and assembles them into the cryptographic core of real on-disk encryption formats. It has three kinds of module:

  • disk-encryption modes (xts, cbc), with assembly kernels ahead of OpenSSL on one core;
  • primitives the standard library lacks (ccm, serpent, camellia, kuznyechik);
  • format cores built on them (zfscrypt).

Everything here is the crypto layer only. Parsing on-disk structures (the ZFS DSL_CRYPTO_KEY bonus area, blkptr_t IV/MAC fields, a LUKS or BitLocker header…) is the job of the format driver that calls into these packages, such as go-fde or go-filesystems.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Module Import path What it does xts github.com/go-encryptions/xts XTS-AES, a drop-in for golang.org/x/crypto/xts with byte-identical output and a fused amd64/arm64 kernel. cbc github.com/go-encryptions/cbc AES-CBC for disk encryption: an 8-block arm64 decryption kernel, and per-sector IVs (eboiv, essiv). ccm github.com/go-encryptions/ccm AES-CCM (Counter with CBC-MAC) AEAD per RFC 3610 / NIST SP 800-38C. Exposes the standard cipher.AEAD interface; fills the gap left by stdlib's GCM-only crypto/cipher. serpent github.com/go-encryptions/serpent The Serpent block cipher as a cipher.Block, bitsliced, in the byte order VeraCrypt uses. camellia github.com/go-encryptions/camellia The Camellia block cipher (RFC 3713) as a cipher.Block, pure Go, big-endian as specified. kuznyechik github.com/go-encryptions/kuznyechik The Kuznyechik block cipher (GOST R 34.12-2015, RFC 7801) as a cipher.Block, pure Go, in the byte order of the RFC and VeraCrypt. zfscrypt github.com/go-encryptions/zfscrypt The cryptographic core of OpenZFS native dataset encryption — PBKDF2 wrapping-key derivation, MEK unwrap, HKDF-SHA512 per-block keys, and AES-CCM/GCM block decryption (read path). Depends on ccm.

docs.title: Design principles
docs.text:
• Few dependencies. The ccm, serpent, cbc and zfscrypt packages import the standard library only, apart from zfscrypt importing this org's ccm. xts adds golang.org/x/sys/cpu for feature detection.
  • Standard interfaces. ccm is a drop-in cipher.AEAD, serpent a cipher.Block, and xts has x/crypto/xts's API.
  • Byte-identical to a reference. Each module is checked against an oracle: crypto/cipher, x/crypto/xts, Botan's Serpent vectors.
  • Measured. The kernels are benchmarked against OpenSSL or Botan on one core, and a gap is filed as an issue.
  • Constant-time verification. Tag comparison uses crypto/subtle; failed authentication wipes scratch plaintext and returns an error with dst unchanged.
  • Crypto, not format. These packages take already-parsed keys, IVs, MACs and AAD and return plaintext. They never touch the disk.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
go-encryptions is a set of pure-Go modules (CGO_ENABLED=0). zfscrypt builds directly on ccm. xts and cbc add assembly kernels for amd64 and arm64, with a portable path everywhere else.

Module Import path Layer What it does xts github.com/go-encryptions/xts mode XTS-AES (IEEE P1619, NIST SP 800-38E), a drop-in for golang.org/x/crypto/xts with byte-identical output. A fused 8-block arm64 kernel, plus DecryptSectors; ahead of OpenSSL on one core. cbc github.com/go-encryptions/cbc mode AES-CBC for disk encryption: an 8-block arm64 decryption kernel, plus per-sector IVs (eboiv, essiv) 8 at a time. Byte-identical to crypto/cipher; ahead of OpenSSL on one core. ccm github.com/go-encryptions/ccm primitive AES-CCM AEAD (RFC 3610 / NIST SP 800-38C). A cipher.AEAD wrapper around any 128-bit block cipher, with configurable nonce (7–13 bytes) and tag (4–16 bytes) sizes. Fills stdlib's CCM gap. zfscrypt github.com/go-encryptions/zfscrypt format core OpenZFS native-encryption primitives: KDF, MEK unwrap, per-block key derivation, AES-CCM/GCM block decrypt. Pure Go, table-driven.

docs.title: Dependency graph
docs.text:
zfscrypt ──► ccm ──► crypto/aes, crypto/cipher (stdlib)
   │
   └──► crypto/pbkdf2, crypto/hkdf, crypto/hmac, crypto/sha1, crypto/sha512 (stdlib)

ccm has zero non-stdlib dependencies. zfscrypt depends on exactly one external module — this org's own ccm — because the Go standard library does not provide CCM.

docs.title: camellia — Camellia block cipher
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/camellia

import "github.com/go-encryptions/camellia"

Package camellia implements the Camellia block cipher (RFC 3713; Aoki, Ichikawa, Kanda, Matsui, Moriai, Nakajima and Tokita) as a standard cipher.Block: 16-byte blocks and 16-, 24- or 32-byte keys. It is pure Go, with no cgo and no dependency beyond the standard library.

Its first consumer is VeraCrypt-volume support in go-fde/veracrypt, which needs Camellia under go-encryptions/xts with 256-bit keys.

docs.title: Byte order
docs.text: Camellia is big-endian by specification: block and key are read as big-endian 64-bit words, so the ciphertext is the same on every architecture.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
func NewCipher(key []byte) (cipher.Block, error)

type KeySizeError int // returned for any key length other than 16, 24, 32

Encrypt and Decrypt follow the cipher.Block contract: dst and src may be the same slice (in-place), and a buffer shorter than 16 bytes panics.

block, err := camellia.NewCipher(key) // camellia.KeySizeError if len(key) is not 16, 24 or 32
if err != nil {
    return err
}
block.Encrypt(ct[:16], pt[:16])

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• The three vectors of RFC 3713 Appendix A (128-, 192- and 256-bit keys).
  • The 17 vectors of Botan's src/tests/data/block/camellia.vec.
  • A differential corpus of 750 random vectors generated from the Botan command line by internal/genbotan.
  • A fuzz test cross-checking Encrypt/Decrypt round trips.
  • 100 % statement coverage, with the race detector, on amd64 and arm64, and under QEMU on big-endian s390x and on riscv64.

See the README for the benchmark against Botan.

docs.title: cbc — AES-CBC for disk encryption
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/cbc

import "github.com/go-encryptions/cbc"

Package cbc implements AES-CBC for disk encryption, with an arm64 kernel that decrypts 8 blocks at a time. Its output is byte-identical to crypto/cipher.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
c, err := cbc.NewCipher(key) // 16, 24 or 32 bytes

c.Decrypt(dst, src, iv)               // one CBC chain
c.DecryptSectors(dst, src, 512, ivs)  // one chain per sector, one IV each
c.EncryptECB(ivs, positions)          // per-sector IVs: eboiv, essiv
c.Encrypt(dst, src, iv)               // through crypto/cipher (serial)

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
CBC decryption is parallel. Each plaintext block is D(C[i]) ^ C[i-1], and every ciphertext block is known before the first one is decrypted. On arm64, crypto/cipher's CBC decrypter does not use that: - it decrypts one block at a time through cipher.Block; - it allocates a 512-byte buffer per call.

This package interleaves the AESD rounds of 8 blocks and keeps every round key in a register, the same kernel shape as xts.

Disk formats give each sector its own IV by encrypting its position: - BitLocker's eboiv is AES_K(byte offset); - LUKS's essiv is AES_{SHA-256(K)}(sector).

EncryptECB computes those IVs 8 at a time, and DecryptSectors takes one IV per sector.

Encryption cannot be parallelised within one chain, because each block needs the previous ciphertext, so Encrypt uses crypto/cipher. On architectures other than arm64, everything goes through crypto/cipher, with the same output.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Decryption on one Apple M4 Max core, from 6 interleaved rounds of abbench --max-load 8. The reference is OpenSSL 3.6.5 on the same core (openssl speed -decrypt -evp aes-*-cbc -bytes N):

crypto/cipher cbc OpenSSL AES-128, 512 B 2.03 GB/s 18.3 GB/s (104 %) 17.6 GB/s AES-128, 4 KiB 2.59 GB/s 20.7 GB/s (101 %) 20.6 GB/s AES-256, 512 B 1.92 GB/s 14.8 GB/s (107 %) 13.8 GB/s AES-256, 4 KiB 2.48 GB/s 15.3 GB/s (118 %) 13.0 GB/s

cbc makes zero allocations per call; crypto/cipher makes one.

docs.title: Checked
docs.text:
• Every path is compared block for block with crypto/cipher: AES-128, -192 and -256; the 8-block groups and the 1–7 block tail; in place or not; the kernel and the portable path. FuzzDecrypt does the same on arbitrary input.
  • Each kernel was broken once on purpose, and the tests failed both times.
  • CI runs on amd64, arm64, riscv64, loong64, ppc64le and big-endian s390x, with 100 % coverage on each.

Its consumer is go-fde/bitlocker (AES-CBC, with and without the Elephant diffuser).

docs.title: ccm — AES-CCM AEAD
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/ccm

import "github.com/go-encryptions/ccm"

Package ccm implements the CCM (Counter with CBC-MAC) AEAD mode specified by RFC 3610 and NIST SP 800-38C, suitable for use with AES (or any 128-bit block cipher).

CCM is not provided by the Go standard library — stdlib's crypto/cipher only exposes GCM. This package fills that gap so callers (in particular the zfscrypt OpenZFS-encryption parser) don't have to depend on golang.org/x/crypto for AES-CCM.

The implementation is pure Go, uses only crypto/aes plus the caller-supplied cipher.Block, and exposes the standard cipher.AEAD interface, so it composes with any code that already understands GCM-style sealed/open.

docs.title: Parameter ranges
docs.text:
Parameter Symbol Allowed values nonce size N [7, 13] (RFC 3610 §3 — encoded as L = 15 − N) tag size M {4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16} plaintext length P len(P) ≤ 2^(8L) − 1

Typical OpenZFS usage is N = 12, M = 16 (L = 3, so the encoded-length field is 3 bytes — sufficient for any ZFS block, which is at most 2²⁴ bytes).

docs.title: API
docs.text:
// NewCCM returns a cipher.AEAD using b in CCM mode with the given
// tag and nonce sizes (bytes). b must have a 16-byte block size;
// tagSize ∈ {4,6,8,10,12,14,16}; nonceSize ∈ [7,13].
func NewCCM(b cipher.Block, tagSize, nonceSize int) (cipher.AEAD, error)

The returned value is a standard cipher.AEAD:

  • NonceSize() int — the configured nonce length.
  • Overhead() int — bytes Seal appends after the ciphertext (the tag).
  • Seal(dst, nonce, plaintext, additionalData []byte) []byte — encrypts and authenticates plaintext, authenticates additionalData, appends the result to dst. The nonce must be NonceSize() bytes and unique per key.
  • Open(dst, nonce, ciphertext, additionalData []byte) ([]byte, error) — verifies and decrypts. On a tag mismatch it returns an error and leaves dst unchanged.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
block, _ := aes.NewCipher(key)          // 16/24/32-byte AES key
aead, err := ccm.NewCCM(block, 16, 12)  // tag=16, nonce=12 (the ZFS profile)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

ct := aead.Seal(nil, nonce, plaintext, aad)
pt, err := aead.Open(nil, nonce, ct, aad)
if err != nil {
    // authentication failed
}

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
CCM combines two AES passes over the same key:

  1. CBC-MAC over B_0 || AAD-blocks || plaintext-blocks produces the authentication tag (computeMAC). B_0 encodes the flags, nonce and plaintext length per RFC 3610 §2.2; AAD is prefixed with its length and each region is zero-padded to a 16-byte boundary.
  2. CTR mode encrypts the plaintext starting at counter 1, and the tag is masked with the counter-0 keystream block (ctrXOR / formatCounter).

Open decrypts into a scratch buffer, recomputes the CBC-MAC, and compares against the recovered tag using crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. On failure the scratch plaintext is zeroed before returning.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Standard library only — crypto/aes, crypto/cipher, crypto/subtle, encoding/binary, errors. No third-party dependencies.
  • Constant-time tag comparison to avoid timing oracles.
  • AEAD-conformant Seal/Open semantics, including the Open-leaves-dst- unchanged-on-failure contract.

Requires Go 1.25 or newer.

docs.title: kuznyechik — Kuznyechik block cipher
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/kuznyechik

import "github.com/go-encryptions/kuznyechik"

Package kuznyechik implements the Kuznyechik block cipher of GOST R 34.12-2015 (RFC 7801) as a standard cipher.Block: 16-byte blocks and 32-byte keys. It is pure Go, with no cgo and no dependency beyond the standard library.

Its first consumer is VeraCrypt-volume support in go-fde/veracrypt, which needs Kuznyechik under go-encryptions/xts with 256-bit keys.

docs.title: Byte order
docs.text: Blocks and keys are the byte strings of RFC 7801 section 5 as printed there: the first byte is the leftmost one. VeraCrypt's kuznyechik.c uses the same arrays (its tables are built from the same l and R, and its first round constant is the RFC's C_1), so the two agree byte for byte. The package loads words explicitly little-endian, so the result is the same on every architecture.

docs.title: Not constant-time
docs.text: The implementation is table-driven (the S-box and the linear transformation are folded into sixteen 256-entry tables). Table look-ups use secret-dependent addresses, so it is not constant-time.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
func NewCipher(key []byte) (cipher.Block, error)

type KeySizeError int // returned for any key length other than 32

Encrypt and Decrypt follow the cipher.Block contract: dst and src may be the same slice (in-place), and a buffer shorter than 16 bytes panics.

block, err := kuznyechik.NewCipher(key) // kuznyechik.KeySizeError if len(key) != 32
if err != nil {
    return err
}
block.Encrypt(ct[:16], pt[:16])

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• RFC 7801 section 5: the S, R and L examples, the round constants and ten round keys, and the encryption and decryption example.
  • The 65 vectors of Botan's src/tests/data/block/kuznyechik.vec.
  • A differential corpus of 500 random vectors generated from the Botan command line by internal/genbotan.
  • A fuzz test cross-checking Encrypt/Decrypt round trips.
  • 100 % statement coverage, with the race detector, on amd64 and arm64, and under QEMU on big-endian s390x and on riscv64.

See the README for the benchmark against Botan.

docs.title: serpent — Serpent block cipher
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/serpent

import "github.com/go-encryptions/serpent"

Package serpent implements the Serpent block cipher (Anderson, Biham and Knudsen, AES finalist) as a standard cipher.Block: 16-byte blocks and 16-, 24- or 32-byte keys. It is pure Go, bitsliced, with no cgo and no dependency beyond the standard library.

Its first consumer is VeraCrypt-volume support in go-fde/veracrypt, which needs Serpent under go-encryptions/xts with 256-bit keys.

docs.title: Byte order
docs.text: There are two conventions for the byte order of Serpent's key, plaintext and ciphertext. This package uses the standard one, the same as Botan, VeraCrypt and the Linux serpent algorithm: block and key are read as little-endian 32-bit words. It does not use the reversed order of Linux's tnepres nor of the original submission's test files.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
func NewCipher(key []byte) (cipher.Block, error)

type KeySizeError int // returned for any key length other than 16, 24, 32

Encrypt and Decrypt follow the cipher.Block contract: dst and src may be the same slice (in-place), and a buffer shorter than 16 bytes panics.

block, err := serpent.NewCipher(key) // serpent.KeySizeError if len(key) is not 16, 24 or 32
if err != nil {
    return err
}
block.Encrypt(ct[:16], pt[:16])

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• All 1047 vectors of Botan's src/tests/data/block/serpent.vec (all three key sizes), which fixes the byte order above.
  • A differential corpus of 750 random vectors generated from the Botan command line by internal/genbotan.
  • A fuzz test cross-checking Encrypt/Decrypt round trips.
  • 100 % statement coverage, with the race detector, on amd64 and arm64, and under QEMU on big-endian s390x.

See the README for the benchmark against Botan.

docs.title: xts — XTS-AES for disk encryption
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/xts

import "github.com/go-encryptions/xts"

Package xts implements the XTS tweakable block-cipher mode (IEEE P1619, NIST SP 800-38E). It is the sector-level mode that LUKS, APFS FileVault 2, BitLocker, VeraCrypt and dm-crypt use.

It is a drop-in replacement for golang.org/x/crypto/xts: same NewCipher / Encrypt / Decrypt API, byte-identical output. The difference is speed. x/crypto/xts drives the block cipher one 16-byte block at a time through cipher.Block. This package has a fused AES-XTS kernel that pipelines several blocks and folds the tweak XOR into the rounds.

docs.title: API
docs.text:
// key is two keys of the block cipher, concatenated (32, 48 or 64 bytes for AES).
c, err := xts.NewCipher(aes.NewCipher, key)

c.Encrypt(ciphertext, plaintext, sectorNum) // one sector; sectorNum is the tweak
c.Decrypt(plaintext, ciphertext, sectorNum)

// Many consecutive sectors in one call: sector firstSector+i is
// ciphertext[i*512:(i+1)*512].
c.DecryptSectors(plaintext, ciphertext, 512, firstSector)
c.EncryptSectors(ciphertext, plaintext, 512, firstSector)
  • Buffers must be a whole number of 16-byte blocks, at least one block long: the x/crypto/xts contract.
  • DecryptSectors and EncryptSectors give exactly what Decrypt and Encrypt give sector by sector. On arm64 they encrypt the tweaks of 8 sectors in one pass, instead of making each sector wait for its own tweak.
  • None of these allocate.
  • Any cipher.Block constructor works. Non-AES ciphers (Twofish, Serpent) take the portable per-block path.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
• On amd64 (AES-NI) and arm64 (ARMv8 AES + NEON), the kernel is Plan 9 assembly. On arm64 it takes 8 blocks at a time, with every round key in a register.
  • Measured on one Apple M4 Max core against OpenSSL 3.6.5 (openssl speed -evp aes-*-xts), with 6 interleaved rounds of abbench --max-load 8. Each figure is the share of OpenSSL's decryption throughput:
Decrypt (one sector per call) DecryptSectors (1 MiB per call) AES-128, 512 B 86 % 112 % AES-128, 4 KiB 99 % 102 % AES-256, 512 B 92 % 117 % AES-256, 4 KiB 103 % 107 %
  • riscv64, loong64, ppc64le and s390x use the same per-block algorithm as x/crypto/xts. The output is identical; only the speed differs.

docs.title: Guarantees
docs.text:
• Byte-identical to golang.org/x/crypto/xts on every architecture. CI checks this, with x/crypto as the reference.
  • No cgo, and no dependencies beyond golang.org/x/sys/cpu (feature detection) and golang.org/x/crypto (tests only).
  • Built and tested on all six 64-bit Go targets, natively or under QEMU, with 100 % statement coverage.

Consumers include go-fde/luks, go-fde/apfs, go-fde/bitlocker and go-fde/veracrypt.

docs.title: zfscrypt — OpenZFS encryption core
docs.text:
github.com/go-encryptions/zfscrypt

import "github.com/go-encryptions/zfscrypt"

Package zfscrypt implements the cryptographic primitives used by OpenZFS native (dataset-level) encryption, as added in OpenZFS 0.8 (2019) and stable since.

This package is the "math" half of ZFS encryption: KDF, MEK unwrap, per-block key derivation, and AES-CCM/GCM block decryption. The "format" half — parsing the DSL_CRYPTO_KEY bonus area and extracting per-block IV/MAC from blkptr_t — lives in the consuming filesystem driver, which already understands those on-disk structures.

Only the read path is currently implemented (the motivating use case, cloud-boot, just needs to pull /boot/vmlinuz and /boot/initrd out of an encrypted root), so Wrap/EncryptBlock are not exposed. Adding them later is straightforward — Seal is already present in the underlying AEADs.

docs.title: References (OpenZFS source tree)
docs.text: module/zfs/zio_crypt.c · module/zfs/dsl_crypt.c · include/sys/zio_crypt.h · include/sys/dsl_crypt.h

docs.title: Algorithms & key schedule
docs.text:
Stage Algorithm Wrapping-key derivation PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1(passphrase, salt, iters, 32) MEK unwrap AES-128/192/256-CCM or GCM AEAD Open Per-block key derivation HKDF-SHA512(mek, salt=blockSalt, info=algName, klen) Block decryption AES-128/192/256-CCM (via ccm) or AES-GCM (stdlib) Metadata auth HMAC-SHA512, truncated to 32 bytes

SHA1 is intentional

The wrapping-key KDF uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, matching what OpenZFS shipped in 0.8. It is part of the on-disk format, not a security choice — do not "upgrade" it without a corresponding format change.

docs.title: Suites
docs.text:
Suite is a uint8 matching the on-disk crypt_algorithm field of a DSL_CRYPTO_KEY object:

Constant Value Key length SuiteInherit 0 — (resolved by the format layer) AES128CCM 1 16 AES192CCM 2 24 AES256CCM 3 32 AES128GCM 4 16 AES192GCM 5 24 AES256GCM 6 32

Helpers: Suite.KeyLen() int, Suite.IsCCM() bool, Suite.String() string.

Fixed sizes (ZFS uses 12-byte IVs and 16-byte MACs uniformly):

const (
    IVSize         = 12 // per-block / unwrap IV
    MACSize        = 16 // authentication tag
    WrappingKeyLen = 32 // always AES-256 wraps the MEK
    WrappedKeySize = 64 // 32-byte MEK || 32-byte HMAC key
)

docs.title: API
docs.text:
// DeriveWrappingKey derives the 32-byte wrapping key from the user
// passphrase via PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1. iters and salt come from the
// DSL_CRYPTO_KEY object.
func DeriveWrappingKey(passphrase, salt []byte, iters int) ([]byte, error)

// Unwrap decrypts the wrapped (MEK || HMAC-key) blob with the
// wrapping key, returning the 32-byte MEK and 32-byte HMAC key.
// suite selects CCM vs GCM; ad must equal the AD the pool used at
// wrap time, or Open fails the tag check.
func Unwrap(suite Suite, wrappingKey, iv, mac, wrapped, ad []byte) (mek, hmacKey []byte, err error)

// DeriveBlockKey derives the per-block data key from the MEK via
// HKDF-SHA512 (salt = per-block randomiser, info = suite.String()).
func DeriveBlockKey(suite Suite, mek, salt []byte) ([]byte, error)

// DecryptBlock authenticates and decrypts one ZFS block with a
// previously-derived per-block key.
func DecryptBlock(suite Suite, key, iv, mac, ciphertext, ad []byte) ([]byte, error)

// HMAC returns HMAC-SHA512 over data, truncated to 32 bytes, using
// the dataset's HMAC key — for metadata that bypasses the AEAD
// layer (e.g. the per-block salt).
func HMAC(hmacKey, data []byte) []byte

docs.title: Read path
docs.text:
// 1. Derive the wrapping key from the passphrase.
wk, err := zfscrypt.DeriveWrappingKey(passphrase, kdfSalt, iters)

// 2. Unwrap the master encryption key (and its HMAC sibling).
mek, hmacKey, err := zfscrypt.Unwrap(suite, wk, wrapIV, wrapMAC, wrapped, wrapAD)

// 3. Per encrypted block: derive its key, then decrypt.
blockKey, err := zfscrypt.DeriveBlockKey(suite, mek, blockSalt)
pt, err := zfscrypt.DecryptBlock(suite, blockKey, blockIV, blockMAC, ciphertext, blockAD)

The IV, MAC, salt and AAD inputs are supplied by the format driver after it parses the DSL_CRYPTO_KEY object and the encrypted block's blkptr_t. Passing the wrong AAD surfaces as a tag-verification failure, not as garbage plaintext.

docs.title: Internals
docs.text: decryptAEAD builds the right AEAD for the suite — ccm.NewCCM(block, 16, 12) for CCM suites or cipher.NewGCMWithNonceSize(block, 12) for GCM — then splices ciphertext || mac back together (ZFS stores the tag separately in the blkptr) and calls Open with the IV as the nonce.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Standard library (crypto/aes, crypto/cipher, crypto/hkdf, crypto/hmac, crypto/pbkdf2, crypto/sha1, crypto/sha512) plus this org's own ccm for the CCM suites. No golang.org/x/crypto.

Requires Go 1.25 or newer.
